author: Al Jazeera English
description:
China says it has lifted nearly 100 million rural people out of extreme poverty over the past decade, through new roads, jobs, subsidies and relocation. In some communities, clean energy also played a role.

In Jinzhai County, Anhui, once one of China's poorest areas, farmer Chen Zheshen survived on corn and his son's income until his son's sudden death plunged him into extreme poverty, which Beijing defines as earning less than $512 a year and being unable to afford necessities.

In 2014, Chen joined a pilot project to install solar panels, funded partly by the government and loans. His now paid-off panels generate more than $400 a year. The scheme later expanded to over four million poor households nationwide.

The World Bank estimated in 2024 that 15 percent of China's population lives on less than $8.30 a day, its threshold for upper-middle-income economies. Local officials say they keep monitoring families at risk of falling back into poverty.

Al Jazeera's Katrina Yu reports fro
title: How solar panels helped one Chinese farmer escape extreme poverty

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping's three-day visit to the US has ended with plenty of ceremony but comparatively little concrete progress. 

The one substantive outcome: an extension of the trade truce, originally due to expire in November, now pushed to January to give both sides more time to negotiate.

President Donald Trump called the visit a success, saying it strengthened his personal relationship with Xi and would benefit the US in the long run, describing it as "very positive for both countries." Xi, for his part, was clear that China has specific aims going into future talks, chiefly being treated more fairly, and laid out guidelines for what matters to Beijing going forward. 

The two leaders are set to meet twice more before year's end: at a summit in China in November, if Trump agrees to attend, and at the G20, to be held at a Trump property in Florida in December.

Al Jazeera's Alan Fisher reports from the White House.

title: Trump and Xi extend trade truce to January after high-profile Washington visit

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Israel's occupation of southern Lebanon has reshaped the region, with the military extensively destroying predominantly Shia villages it views as Hezbollah's support base. Nearby Christian villages have been told they will be spared the same demolition policy if they remain neutral in the conflict, but life there is still far from normal.

In Marjayoun district, residents describe a paralysed economy. A journey from Beirut that once took about 90 minutes now takes over three hours because of the occupation.

Families in nearby Qlayaa describe nightly explosions shaking their homes, shattering windows and keeping children from school, along with water, electricity and healthcare shortages. Residents say they need major assistance to keep living there.

Even away from the occupied areas, Israel's campaign has upended lives, leaving what one resident calls isolated pockets surrounded by ruins.

Al Jazeera's Zeina Khodr reports from Marjayoun district, Lebanon.

Subscribe to our channel:
title: In southern Lebanon, Shia villages lie in ruins as Christian towns struggle in neutrality

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi confirmed late Friday that Tehran has given the US a proposal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying Washington now has the choice. 

The plan revives the deal that collapsed in June, but cuts the timeline from 60 days to seven: fighting would stop on all fronts, including Lebanon; Washington would lift its blockade, waive oil sanctions and release frozen Iranian funds, the strait would reopen by day six, and talks on Iran's nuclear programme would begin on day seven.

Washington has yet to respond. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott told Al Jazeera, "I'm not going to negotiate through the media. But the president holds all the cards here." Iran has meanwhile been working multiple diplomatic channels: 

Araghchi is reportedly staying in New York until Monday, awaiting a response, as the war enters its eighth month.

Al Jazeera's Gabriel Elizondo reports from the United Nations.

title: Iran's foreign minister waits in New York for a US response

The party of Pakistan's former prime minister, Imran Khan, has called off protests planned for this weekend in Islamabad demanding his release from prison, where he has been held since 2023. Instead, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf says it will march from Peshawar to Islamabad on October 5.

Police had been preparing to block the weekend protests, sealing roads into the capital with shipping containers at every entry and exit point, including routes from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. 

PTI says its right to protest is enshrined in Pakistan's constitution and insists it will keep pushing for the release of Khan, whom it considers a political prisoner. The government maintains he was convicted by the courts for crimes he committed.

Al Jazeera's Osama bin Javid reports from Islamabad.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Gangs continue to terrorise Haiti, with 30 people recently killed in an attack in Kenscoff, just outside Port-au-Prince. One resident says the government does nothing to protect people. 

Haiti's police remain outnumbered and outgunned, and the international response, a multinational Gang Suppression Force authorised by the UN Security Council a year ago to replace a Kenyan-led mission, has seen only a fraction of its planned troops deployed.

For 13 years, UN peacekeepers served under MINUSTAH, helping stabilise the country and strengthen police, but leaving a controversial legacy that included sexual abuse allegations and a cholera epidemic. 

With elections planned for December, Haiti's first national vote in about a decade, this new, more targeted mission aims to help local forces confront gangs and secure the country enough for people to vote.

Al Jazeera's Teresa Bo reports.
